name: Joint RF-context-gen + bridge-future-pred for AR rollout stability

description: BASELINE: standard Brownian-bridge forecaster (JOINT_GEN=0, TECHNIQUE=none), jit3d-128/4/4 PHW8, 4500 steps/220 traj, SEED=0, dt=0.024, vloss sigma=0.3 wclamp=10, fp32, AVG4. Reproduces prior reference exactly (ED 951). The number to beat with the joint RF-context-gen + bridge-future-pred head.

asi.hypothesis: baseline reference; joint RF-ctx-gen head should lower rollout_ed via stronger on-manifold prior + robustness to context drift
asi.regime: dt=0.024 (moderate-fast) where bridge>>RF is established; RF develops artifacts here

description: joint-gen v1 (JOINT_GEN=1, weight=1.0, couple lead=0.3, decouple, all slots): WORSE. ED 1141 vs baseline 951, sharpness 0.89 (blur), mass_drift 0.047. Context-recon objective at full weight dilutes future prediction + mildly corrupts dynamics conditioning.

asi.hypothesis: joint RF-ctx-gen head with user defaults (couple lead=0.3, decouple, weight 1.0, all slots) would lower rollout_ed via generative prior
asi.next_action_hint: lower JOINT_CTX_WEIGHT (0.1-0.3) so future loss dominates; possibly larger JOINT_LEAD (gentler context noise); test JOINT_LAST_ONLY
asi.result: WORSE: ED 1141 vs baseline 951, sharpness 0.89 (blur), mass_drift 0.047
asi.why: context weight 1.0 makes RF context-recon co-equal with future pred -> dilutes dynamics; RF-noising context at s in [0.3,1] degrades conditioning (esp low t, s=0.3=70% noise)

description: joint-gen weight=0.1 (lead=0.3, decouple, all slots): WORSE than weight=1.0. ED 1417 (vs 1141@w1.0, 951 baseline). Per-frame quality better (sharp 0.95) but rollout drifts more. Counterintuitive: higher context weight = more drift-robust. Weak prior + noised context = worst of both.

asi.finding: weight sweep is COUNTERINTUITIVE: weight 1.0 -> ED 1141 (better), weight 0.1 -> ED 1417 (worse). Higher weight = more drift-robust (lower ED) but blurrier (sharp 0.89 vs 0.95). At low weight the model sees noised context but has a weak prior -> worst of both worlds.
asi.core_tension: RF-noising the context that conditions future prediction degrades dynamics conditioning (bridge needs clean-ish context); the generative prior must be strong enough to overcome this
asi.next_action_hint: try JOINT_LAST_ONLY=1 (keep dynamics-bearing older slot clean, noise only the recent slot that drifts at inference) - matches ctx_bridge finding that last-only small noise helped the bridge

description: joint-gen last-only WIN (weight=1.0, lead=0.3, decouple, LAST_ONLY=1): ED 766 (-19% vs 951), ed_late 707 (-29%). Keeping older dynamics slot clean + RF-noising only the recent (drift-prone) slot robustifies rollout. Tradeoff: sharpness 0.80 (blur), mass_drift 0.10. First joint-gen config to beat baseline.

asi.breakthrough: JOINT_LAST_ONLY=1 is the key: ED 766 (-19%), ed_late 707 (-29%) vs baseline 951/1002. RF-noising ONLY the recent context slot (the one that drifts at inference), keeping the older dynamics-bearing slot clean, robustifies the rollout.
asi.mechanism: model jointly denoises recent slot (generative prior) + predicts future from [clean-old, noised-recent]; matches ctx_bridge finding that last-only small context noise helped the bridge
asi.tradeoff: sharpness 1.02->0.80 (blur), mass_drift 0.009->0.10. ED win is positional stability (pooled 6x6 features match) despite worse texture (grad/lap) + mass. Real stability win with quality cost.
asi.next_action_hint: tune to recover sharpness: sweep JOINT_LEAD (gentler recent-slot noise e.g. 0.5), weight; the recent-slot RF recon pulls toward mean -> blur. Also consider coupling the recent-slot noise to be small.

description: joint-gen last-only lead=0.5 (w=1.0): ED 755 (-0.5% vs best 766, -20.5% vs baseline). Quality recovered: sharp 0.80->0.85, mass 0.10->0.082. But ed_late 707->806 (worse late stability). Gentler recent-slot noise trades late-stability for early-ED + sharpness.

asi.finding: lead sweep (last-only, w=1.0): lead 0.3 -> ED 766/sharp0.80/mass0.10/ed_late707; lead 0.5 -> ED 755/sharp0.85/mass0.082/ed_late806. Gentler recent-slot noise improves early ED + quality but WORSENS late stability (ed_late 707->806).
asi.tension: lower lead (more recent-slot noise) = better late-rollout stability but blurrier; higher lead = better early ED + sharpness but worse late. Sweet spot search continues.
asi.next: try lead 0.7 (even gentler) to map the curve; then pick the ED-optimal lead and recover sharpness another way

description: joint-gen last-only lead=0.7: CATASTROPHIC (ED 1509, ed_late 2454). Non-monotonic cliff vs lead 0.3/0.5. lead is a noisy knob — stop tuning it. Robust win = last-only + lead∈[0.3,0.5].

asi.finding: lead=0.7 CATASTROPHIC: ED 1509, ed_late 2454, sharp 0.74, mass 0.21. Non-monotonic cliff (0.3->766, 0.5->755, 0.7->1509). lead is a NOISY/chaotic knob - do NOT fine-tune it. Gentle noise (s in [0.7,1]) barely regularizes but shifts model into bad optimum.
asi.robust_win: last-only + lead in [0.3,0.5] beats baseline 951->755. This structural choice (not the exact lead) is the robust finding.
asi.next: stop tuning lead. Recover sharpness via weight (gentler prior keeps noising-robustness) or decouple=0. Then VALIDATE champion on SEED=1 (anti-overfit) since all tuning is on SEED=0.
asi.overfit_warning: single-seed (SEED=0) tuning on a chaotic benchmark risks overfitting; must cross-seed-validate the champion

description: joint-gen weight=0.5 (lead0.5, last-only): CATASTROPHIC ED 1725. Confirms weight is a noisy knob too. Only w=1.0 last-only lead[0.3,0.5] robust. Pivoting to user's structural request: bridge for BOTH context+future (not HP fishing).

asi.finding: weight=0.5 (lead 0.5, last-only) CATASTROPHIC: ED 1725, ed_late 3010. weight is ALSO a noisy knob (w0.1 allslots 1417, w0.5 lastonly 1725, w1.0 lastonly 755). Only w=1.0 last-only lead[0.3,0.5] is robust.
asi.overfit_risk: HIGH - 7 runs all SEED=0, lead AND weight are noisy/chaotic knobs. Hyperparameter search is fitting noise.
asi.user_pivot: switch context interpolant from RF to Brownian BRIDGE (bridge for BOTH ctx+fut). Structural change, not HP fishing. Bridge clean-endpoint may fix blur (RF ctx recon mean-pulls -> blur; bridge vloss forces sharp data-end recon). Backed by FINDINGS bridge>>RF for stability.
asi.champion: lead0.5/last-only/w1.0 ED755 sharp0.85 (still champion after this discard)

description: bridge-for-context sigma=0.3 (last-only, lead0.5, w1.0): ED 1195, WORSE than RF-context 755. Extra Brownian noise degrades conditioning. Blur unchanged (sharp 0.85 = RF). Bridge does not fix blur.

asi.finding: bridge-context (sigma=0.3) WORSE than RF-context: ED 1195 vs 755. Bridge adds extra mid-path Brownian noise (c_s eta) that RF lacks -> degrades future-pred conditioning. BLUR NOT FIXED: sharpness 0.85 identical to RF-context. User's hypothesis (bridge clean-endpoint fixes blur) FALSIFIED - blur is inherent to the joint-noising of the recent context slot, not the context interpolant.
asi.conclusion_tentative: RF context is cleaner (no extra noise term) and beats bridge context at equal sigma. Testing bridge sigma=0.1 (minimal extra noise) as fair final check; if it loses to RF 755, RF context is the winner.
asi.blur_source: the noising of the recent context slot itself (model relies on older slot + averages) regardless of RF vs bridge interpolant

description: bridge-for-both sigma=0.1 NEW BEST: ED 642.77 (-32% vs baseline 951, -15% vs RF-ctx 755), sharpness 0.95 (recovered from 0.85). Bridge clean-endpoint fixes blur when context sigma small. User's bridge-for-both idea confirmed; context sigma=0.1 is the key.

asi.breakthrough2: bridge-for-context with SMALL sigma=0.1 is NEW BEST: ED 642.77 (-32% vs baseline 951, -15% vs RF-context 755), ed_late 717, sharpness 0.95 (RECOVERED from RF's 0.85!), mass 0.078. User's 'bridge for both' intuition CONFIRMED - context sigma just needs to be small (0.1 not 0.3).
asi.mechanism: bridge sigma 0.3 -> too much extra Brownian noise (ED 1195); sigma 0.1 -> minimal extra noise + bridge clean-endpoint landing + one-sided vloss weight forces SHARP data-end recon (fixes blur 0.85->0.95) AND best stability (ED 642<755). Sweet spot.
asi.champion_config: JOINT_GEN=1 CTX_FLOW=bridge CTX_BRIDGE_SIGMA=0.1 LAST_ONLY=1 LEAD=0.5 COUPLE=1 DECOUPLE=1 CTX_WEIGHT=1.0
asi.sigma_sensitivity: 0.3->1195 (bad), 0.1->642 (great). HIGH sensitivity -> MUST cross-seed validate (SEED=1) to rule out overfit to SEED=0
asi.next: cross-seed validate champion on SEED=1 (anti-overfit, highest priority); then sweep sigma 0.05/0.15 around 0.1

description: CONTROL: SEED=1 baseline (JOINT_GEN=0) ED 1220 (harder seed than SEED=0's 951). Reference for cross-seed validation of the bridge-ctx champion.

asi.control: SEED=1 BASELINE (JOINT_GEN=0): ED 1220, ed_late 1211, sharp 1.06, mass 0.024. SEED=1 is HARDER than SEED=0 (951). Reference for cross-seed champion validation.
asi.purpose: anti-overfit control - need champion on SEED=1 to beat this 1220 to confirm the joint-gen win generalizes beyond SEED=0
